title: Finitely presented affine replacement with an overlap isomorphism
statement: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], W a quasi-compact open [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], V an affine open, and H a quasi-coherent module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose H restricted to W is finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. There exists a finitely presented module E on V and a map j from E to H restricted to V whose restriction to W intersect V is an isomorphism. No extension away from V and no glued module is asserted.

proof.text: Work on the affine scheme V. The intersection W intersect V is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness and compactness of affine opens. Restrict the finite presentation on W to the overlap, using the canonical restriction identifications.

Apply finite-type submodule extension to H restricted to V, using its whole finite-type restriction on the overlap. This gives a finite-type quasi-coherent H-prime contained in H restricted to V, with equal restriction on the overlap.

Take a finite free epimorphism onto H-prime using its affine global generators. Its kernel K is quasi-coherent. Restriction preserves kernels and epimorphisms. The restricted target is finitely presented, so Modules 01BP says that K restricted to the overlap is finite type.

Apply finite-type submodule extension to K and its whole restriction on the overlap, producing K-prime. The cokernel E of K-prime mapping to the finite free source is finitely presented by Modules 0H96. Since K-prime is contained in the kernel, the epimorphism descends to a map E to H-prime and then H. On the overlap K-prime equals K; an epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel, so the restricted induced map is an isomorphism. Transport E and its map back to the localized site over V.
